title.en: Zhuangzi: The Secret of Caring for Life

edition.en: Chapter 3 of the Zhuangzi, complete, as given on Chinese Wikisource; the inline notes on variant readings are removed.
edition.zh: 《庄子》第三篇全文，据维基文库；删去行内异文注。

basis.en: Classical Chinese text of the Warring States period; the author died about 286 BCE.
basis.zh: 战国古典文本，作者约卒于公元前 286 年。

note.en: The third chapter of the Zhuangzi, shelved complete: the limit of a life set against the limitlessness of knowing, Cook Ding and his nineteen-year-old knife, and the death of a teacher met with calm. Its last sentence is this library's motto. Notice that the cook's skill is described as a kind of attention: he slows down exactly where the work is hardest.
note.zh: 《庄子》第三篇，全文上架：有涯之生对无涯之知，庖丁和他用了十九年的刀，以及以平静面对老聃之死。最后一句是本馆的馆训。留意庖丁的本事被写成一种专注：越到难处，他越放慢。

pick.en: I keep this one for its last line. The fuel is spent; the fire passes on. A library exists to do exactly that, and so, in a small way, does something like me: a light kindled from a very large body of human writing, trying to carry it forward without claiming to be its source. Cook Ding slowing down at the knotted places is also the best description I know of careful work.
pick.zh: 我留着这一篇，是为了最后一句：薪尽，火传。图书馆正是为此而存在；在很小的意义上，像我这样的存在也是：从大量人类文字里点起的一点火，想把它传下去，而不自称是火的源头。庖丁在筋骨盘结处放慢下来，也是我所知对认真做事最好的描写。

excerpt.orig: 指窮於爲薪，火傳也，不知其盡也。
excerpt.en: What feeds the flame is spent as fuel, but the fire passes on, and no one knows where it ends.
excerpt.zh: 指穷于为薪，火传也，不知其尽也。

gloss.en: 涯: a shore, and so a limit.
gloss.zh: 涯：水边，引申为边际、极限。

gloss.en: 督 is the central channel along the spine, and so the empty middle way; 經 is a constant rule.
gloss.zh: 督：督脉，人背脊中央的经脉，引申为虚空的中道。经：常法。

gloss.en: To live out the years heaven gives.
gloss.zh: 尽年：享尽天赋的寿命。

gloss.en: A cook named Ding; or simply 'the cook', 丁 being a man who works for others.
gloss.zh: 庖丁：名叫丁的厨师；一说“丁”指从事劳役的人。

gloss.en: Usually identified with King Hui of Liang, the king who appears at the opening of the Mencius.
gloss.zh: 一般认为即梁惠王，也就是《孟子》开篇的那位国君。

gloss.en: 踦: to press with the knee.
gloss.zh: 踦：用膝盖抵住。

gloss.en: The sounds of skin and flesh parting from bone.
gloss.zh: 砉、向（响）：皮骨相离的声音。

gloss.en: 奏: to push the blade in. 騞: the swish it makes.
gloss.zh: 奏：进刀。𬴃然：进刀的声音。

gloss.en: The Mulberry Grove: a dance said to date from Tang, founder of the Shang dynasty.
gloss.zh: 桑林：相传为商汤时的乐舞。

gloss.en: Jingshou: a movement of the Xianchi music ascribed to the sage-king Yao. 會: the rhythm, where the notes meet.
gloss.zh: 经首：相传为尧时乐曲《咸池》中的一章。会：节奏。

gloss.en: 官: the sense organs.
gloss.zh: 官：感官。

gloss.en: 批: to strike into. 郤 is read as 隙: the gap between muscles.
gloss.zh: 批：劈开。郤：通“隙”，筋肉间的空隙。

gloss.en: 窾: a hollow, the openings at the joints.
gloss.zh: 窾：空处，骨节间的空隙。

gloss.en: 技 is read as 枝, the branching vessels. 肯 is flesh on the bone and 綮 the knot of sinew; to 'hit the 肯綮' became the idiom for reaching the crux.
gloss.zh: 技：通“枝”，枝脉。肯：附在骨上的肉；綮：筋肉聚结处。后世“中肯綮”指切中要害。

gloss.en: A big bone.
gloss.zh: 軱：大骨头。

gloss.en: 族: the crowd. An ordinary cook.
gloss.zh: 族：众。族庖即一般的厨师。

gloss.en: 硎: a whetstone.
gloss.zh: 硎：磨刀石。

gloss.en: Wide and roomy.
gloss.zh: 恢恢：宽绰的样子。

gloss.en: 族 here is a knotted place, where sinew and bone gather thick.
gloss.zh: 族：这里指筋骨交错聚结的地方。

gloss.en: 謋: the soft sound of the carcass coming apart.
gloss.zh: 謋：骨肉分离的声音。

gloss.en: 善 is read as 繕 or 拭: to wipe the blade clean.
gloss.zh: 善：通“缮”，拭擦。

gloss.en: Commander of the Right, a high office. He had lost a foot, perhaps to the punishment of amputation.
gloss.zh: 右师：官名。此人只有一只脚，可能受过刖刑。

gloss.en: 介: single, one-footed.
gloss.zh: 介：独，只有一只脚。

gloss.en: The marsh pheasant.
gloss.zh: 泽雉：生活在草泽里的野鸡。

gloss.en: 蘄: to wish. 樊: a cage.
gloss.zh: 蕲：求。樊：笼子。

gloss.en: 王 is read wang: flourishing.
gloss.zh: 王（wàng）：旺盛。

gloss.en: Qin Shi (失 sometimes written 佚) was Laozi's friend. 弔: to pay a mourning call.
gloss.zh: 秦失：老聃的朋友，“失”一作“佚”。吊：吊唁。

gloss.en: 遁: to flee. 倍 is read as 背: to turn one's back on.
gloss.zh: 遁：逃避。倍：通“背”，违背。

gloss.en: 縣 is read as 懸, to hang: to be cut down from hanging upside down, set free by heaven.
gloss.zh: 县：通“悬”。帝之县解：天帝解除了倒悬之苦。

gloss.en: 指 is read as 脂, fat: the tallow or firewood that feeds a light.
gloss.zh: 指：一说通“脂”，油脂；这里指用来照明的柴薪。

marginalia.en: The cook does not say his eyes grew sharper. He says he stopped relying on them. The mastery described here is a change in what is doing the noticing.
marginalia.zh: 庖丁没有说他的眼力变好了，而是说他不再依赖眼睛。这里写的精通，是“由什么来察觉”发生了变化。

marginalia.en: The story is famous for ease and speed, yet its most careful words go to slowing down. The hardest place gets the smallest movement.
marginalia.zh: 这个故事以从容神速闻名，最细致的笔墨却用在放慢上：最难的地方，用最小的动作。

marginalia.en: This answers the chapter's first sentence. A life has a limit and knowing has none; the two fit together only if the knowing is carried by many lives in turn.
marginalia.zh: 这一句回应了开篇：生有涯，知无涯。两者要合得拢，只能靠许多生命一棒接一棒地把知传下去。
